text:
Alice M: Heads-up — CI on main is red after this morning's poetry lock update. Install step is hanging in the pip resolver (seems stuck on resolving a transitive subdep). Anyone seen this pattern before?

CI Bot: pipeline #4521 failed: job=build/install step=poetry-install duration=00:12:34 — exit_code=1

Ben T: Can you paste the install logs (the resolver section)?

Alice M: pasted below (trimmed):
```
  Resolving dependencies...
  Found cyclic or long resolution path for: rfc3986 (from httpx -> httpcore -> multidict?)
  Still trying: aiohttp, httpcore, rfc3986
  Waiting for backtracking to finish (this can take a while)
  Exception: ResolutionError: Could not find a compatible set of versions for package rfc3986
```

Charlie R: ugh. sounds like a transitive pin/constraint got tightened. Did the lockfile bump include any rfc3986/uri-parser changes?

Alice M: The lock update commit is 1a2b3c4 (from the dependency bot). Diff shows rfc3986 pinned to 1.5.0 -> 1.6.0 and httpcore moved to a new minor.

Dana (devops): Quick triage plan: 1) try a local install `poetry install --no-root -vvv` to reproduce, 2) try `poetry lock --no-update` to see if lockfile itself is malformed, 3) if reproduced, we can bisect which subdep change caused it. Who can run 1?

Ben T: I'll run a repro locally and paste logs. If it's resolver hang, I can try `pip-compile` approach to narrow down (or a small env with just httpx/httpcore).

Alice M: thanks. repro steps I used: `git checkout main && git pull && poetry install --no-root -vvv` (containerized runner).

Charlie R: If bisect needed, we should bisect on the lockfile changeset range rather than source commits. Maybe do a binary search over the dependency-bot PRs. I have a small script to swap lockfile entries and run `poetry install` — saved me time before.

Dana (devops): Ben, if you can confirm, I can schedule an emergency revert of the lock update (revert the merge commit) and re-run CI to buy time. But prefer to identify the minimal culprit first.

Ben T: Repro'd locally. Same hang at resolver. I ran `pip index versions rfc3986` and found 1.6.0 was yanked on PyPI (??) — that could explain backtracking oddities. Also trying `poetry lock --no-update` gave a different hash.

Alice M: If PyPI yanked a version, we should either pin to older release or instruct poetry to prefer compatible. Quick fix: revert lock update so main is green, then we can coordinate a proper pin/patch.

Charlie R: Alternatively, add an explicit constraint in pyproject: `rfc3986 = "~=1.5"` to avoid 1.6. That will lock to 1.5.x without a full revert. But that still needs a PR and QA.

Dana (devops): I'm going to queue a revert PR for the lockfile now so CI can go green. If Ben confirms reverting fixes local, we'll merge fast. @Ben T can you test reverting locally and post result?

Ben T: Reverted to previous lockfile locally (checked out commit before 1a2b3c4). `poetry install` completed fine, unit tests started running. Re-run CI after revert should pass.

Alice M: Thank you — please include the revert PR link here when ready. Also add a short note to the changelog so we remember to follow up with a proper resolution.

Dana (devops): Revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/commit/ff9e8d7 (PR #2387). CI rerun queued. :thumbsup:

CI Bot: pipeline #4522 queued due to PR #2387 (revert lockfile).

Alice M: Great. Post-mortem action: we need a checklist for lock bumps: smoke run of `poetry install` with `--no-root` + a small resolver stress test on CI before merging. I'll draft a tiny RFC.

Charlie R: Agreed. Also let's add a step: check if any newly pinned versions are yanked on PyPI (we can query index) — could be automated in the dep-bot.

Ben T: For follow-up, I can run a bisect on the dependency bump PRs to identify exactly which package bump triggered the resolver pathologies, if we want the root cause. Otherwise revert buys us time.

Dana (devops): I'll keep an eye on #2387 CI. If it goes green, I'll merge and then open a follow-up ticket to do the bisect and add the pre-merge smoke tests.

Alice M: Thanks all.
